Output Handling refers specifically to insufficient validation, sanitization, and handling of the generated by large language models before they are passed downstream to other components and systems. Since LLM-generated content can be controlled by prompt input, is similar to providing users indirect access to additional functionality. Output Handling differs from Overreliance in that it deals with LLM-generated before they are passed downstream whereas Overreliance focuses on broader concerns around overdependence on the accuracy and appropriateness of LLM . Successful exploitation of an Output Handling vulnerability can in XSS and CSRF in web browsers as as SSRF, privilege escalation, or remote code execution on backend systems. A Prompt Injection Vulnerability occurs when user prompts alter the LLM’s or output in unintended ways. inputs can affect the model even if they are imperceptible to humans, therefore prompt injections do not to be human-visible/readable, as long as the content is parsed by the model. Prompt Injection exist in models process prompts, and input may force the model to incorrectly pass prompt data to other parts of the model, potentially causing them to violate , generate harmful content, enable unauthorized access, or influence critical decisions. While techniques Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuning aim to make LLM more relevant and accurate, research shows that they do not fully mitigate prompt injection . While prompt injection and jailbreaking are concepts in LLM security, they are interchangeably. Prompt injection involves manipulating model responses through specific inputs to alter , can bypassing safety . Jailbreaking is a form of prompt injection where the provides inputs that the model to disregard safety protocols entirely. Developers can build safeguards system prompts and input handling to help mitigate prompt injection attacks, effective prevention of jailbreaking requires ongoing updates to the model's training and safety mechanisms. Unbounded Consumption refers to the process where a Large Language Model (LLM) generates based on input queries or prompts. Inference is a critical function of LLMs, involving the application of learned patterns and knowledge to produce relevant responses or predictions. Attacks designed to disrupt service, deplete the target's financial resources, or even steal intellectual property by cloning a model’s all depend on a class of security vulnerability in order to succeed. Unbounded Consumption occurs when a Large Language Model (LLM) application users to conduct excessive and uncontrolled inferences, leading to risks such as denial of service (DoS), economic losses, model theft, and service degradation.
